title: The Real Result Type
story: You ordered a package online. The delivery person arrives — and either hands you the box (success) or gives you a reason why not (error). Result[T, E] captures exactly this: both the outcome and the why.
why: Result[T, E] is XIOM's built-in error handling type — it forces you to handle both success and failure paths, replacing fragile error codes and silent crashes with explicit, type-safe handling.
analogy: Result is like a delivery — either you get the package (Ok) or a note explaining why not (Err). You always know what happened AND why.
try_it: Create a Result with a different error type — make `Result[Str, Int]` where Ok contains a message and Err contains an error code. Match on it and handle both cases differently.
tips: Result[T, E] always needs two type parameters — T for success, E for error
Use `Str` as the error type when you want readable error messages
Match handles both Ok and Err — the compiler ensures you never forget the failure case
common_mistakes: Using Option for error cases — if you need to say WHY something failed, use Result
Writing `Result[Int]` with only one type parameter — Result always needs T AND E
Swapping Ok and Err — `Ok` means success, `Err` means failure; don't return `Err("Everything worked!")`
